title: Measuring system performance
notes: Measure a reproducible operation before changing configuration. PAL summarizes requestor resource consumption; Database Trace examines SQL; Performance Profiler traces procedural rule execution; PDC aggregates runtime health. Choose the tool for the evidence required.

PAL uses continuously collected statistics with little additional collection cost. Reset before a focused scenario and take incremental readings around individual interactions. DELTA readings isolate changes; TOTAL reflects accumulated work. Compare equivalent warm/cold runs rather than unrelated totals.

Database Trace records database operations, timings and related details. Use targeted short traces because collection adds overhead. Investigate expensive queries and commits in context; stack traces add further cost and should be collected only when needed.

Performance Profiler records activities, Data Transforms and When rule execution. It adds substantial overhead. Start, reproduce, stop and analyze; separate inclusive time from time excluding called children to avoid double-counting cost.

Pega Diagnostic Center provides aggregated application health, alerts and trends. Correlate events for the same time and interaction, prioritize recurring issues, and confirm improvements after a change. Monitoring evidence supports diagnosis but does not automatically repair every application defect.
examples: For a slow address form, first capture PAL around opening that form. If database time dominates, narrow the investigation with Database Trace rather than collecting every available trace.
Reset PAL, open the lookup form, add a reading, submit it and add another reading. Compare the expensive DELTA with the same scenario after optimization.
Trace one slow search, stop immediately, sort by elapsed time and inspect the most expensive statement's predicate and execution plan.
Profile a suspected mapping activity, then compare its own CPU time with the time spent in called processing. Do not add both inclusive totals as if they were independent.
A deployment increases repeated slow-query alerts. Correlate the deployment time and affected interaction, diagnose the query and verify that the event rate drops after correction.
pitfalls: Tool mismatch
Profiler identifies every network and SQL root cause alone.
Use PAL to narrow the cause, then the relevant detailed tool.
Tracing cost
Run detailed tracing indefinitely on live traffic.
Scope collection and stop it promptly.
questions: A form is slow but the bottleneck is not known. Which first step provides focused resource evidence?
Measure a reproducible interaction with PAL
Increase all thread counts blindly
Trace every production session indefinitely
Rewrite the UI without measuring
A scoped baseline identifies which resources dominate. Blind changes can worsen or conceal the cause.
PAL contains work from many unrelated interactions. How should a focused measurement begin?
Reset data and take readings around the target interaction
Compare unrelated totals only
Delete all alerts
Raise the pass threshold
Reset and incremental readings isolate the scenario from earlier cumulative work.
Which PAL reading isolates the change since the preceding reading?
DELTA
Only the portal title
A ruleset skim
An attachment category
DELTA represents accumulated statistics since the preceding reading; TOTAL is broader accumulated data.
PAL indicates excessive database time. Which tool gives detailed SQL operations and timings?
Database Trace
Field-level auditing alone
A worklist
A product preview
Database Trace records SQL-related operations and elapsed cost for a targeted database investigation.
Why should a Database Trace run be short and focused?
It produces substantial output and adds diagnostic overhead
SQL never takes time
The tool changes every business rule
It only records the first query forever
Detailed trace collection can affect performance. Collect the relevant scenario and stop, rather than treating it as cost-free monitoring.
An activity spends time in several called Data Transforms. Which tool can expose procedural execution timings?
Performance Profiler
Only Assignment Ready
A local property list
A ruleset password
The Profiler traces activities, Data Transforms and When rules, helping locate procedural bottlenecks.
Which TWO make a Profiler result more reliable to interpret?
Stop collection after reproducing the scenario
Distinguish inclusive time from time excluding children
Add every nested inclusive total together
Assume the trace has no overhead
Stopping limits overhead; understanding inclusive versus own time prevents double-counting called processing.
Operations needs recurring alert trends across application interactions. Which tool is most relevant?
Pega Diagnostic Center
Only one user's Field Value list
A case type label
A Product export
PDC aggregates runtime monitoring and helps correlate recurring events beyond a single local diagnostic run.

title: Reviewing log files
notes: The PEGA log contains operational information, warnings and errors. ALERT contains threshold-based performance events; ALERTSECURITY contains security alerts. Additional logs depend on configured appenders, such as BIX extracts or security-event logging. Capture timestamp, node and requestor context before correlating evidence.

An alert identifies a threshold or security event, not a fully established root cause. My Alerts focuses on session events by default; broader logs and PDC provide wider context. Use event frequency and affected interactions to prioritize investigation, while avoiding unnecessary sensitive data in diagnostics.
examples: A failed connector at 14:10 has an exception in PEGA. A slow report around the same time has an ALERT event; correlate them rather than assuming all log types represent the same failure.
One slow operation among many requests and repeated slow operations for nearly every user need different priorities. Check the interaction and recurrence in PDC before choosing a fix.
pitfalls: Alert versus cause
Every threshold breach proves that the database is faulty.
Correlate timings and context before deciding the cause.
Log scopes
My Alerts always shows every session on every node.
Distinguish the session view from broader system logs.
questions: A developer needs an application exception and operational warning. Which log is the starting point?
PEGA log
Only the theme stylesheet
Only the Product manifest
Only the quiz record
The PEGA/system log records operational information, warnings and errors.
A database operation exceeds a performance threshold. Which log contains the related performance alert?
ALERT
Only BIX extract output
Only a field audit table
Only a work queue name
ALERT records performance-related threshold events. BIX output serves an extraction-specific purpose.
Which log is associated with security alert events?
ALERTSECURITY
Only a local Field Value
Only the ruleset archive
Only the portal history
ALERTSECURITY records security alerts. Other security event logs can also exist depending on configured appenders.
Which TWO help correlate a user's report with diagnostic logs?
The approximate timestamp and requestor/operator context
The affected node and interaction when available
Only the operator's favorite color
Only the certification score
Time, requestor, node and interaction narrow the relevant events and avoid mixing unrelated failures.
An alert threshold is exceeded once. What is the safe interpretation?
Investigate its context; the alert alone does not establish the root cause
Immediately rewrite every rule
Declare every database index invalid
Assume the application must be offline
Alerts flag conditions for investigation. Root-cause analysis requires context and related measurements.
My Alerts initially shows which scope?
The current session's alerts by default
All events in all external systems automatically
Only the next year's events
Only product exports
The session-oriented default differs from broader system logs and monitoring aggregation.
Which evidence helps prioritize two otherwise similar performance alerts?
Recurrence rate and impact on the affected interaction
The length of the log filename alone
The portal icon
The number of case stages regardless of impact
Frequency and user impact provide context for prioritization. A filename is not an impact measurement.
An exception message contains customer identifiers. What should diagnostic handling consider?
Restrict access and avoid unnecessary sensitive data in logs
Publish all details in a public error banner
Ignore permissions because logs are technical
Copy all credentials into the message
Diagnostics can expose sensitive information. Provide useful evidence with appropriate access and data minimization.

title: Debugging system performance
notes: A slow interaction can arise in the client, application server, rule processing, database or external service. Reproduce the reported path and use guardrail warnings plus measured evidence. A high compliance score is useful but does not prove the absence of performance defects.

Rule assembly generates and compiles executable code for rules; rule caches avoid repeating resolution and retrieval. Newly deployed rules can make initial use slower. Compare cold and warm behavior; numerous distinct ruleset lists can increase cache resource demands.

Use PAL deltas to locate database cost, then inspect expensive statements with Database Trace and database tools. Consider filters, indexes, reporting-property optimization, data volume and transaction boundaries. Do not add arbitrary indexes or expose sensitive columns without analyzing the query and data requirements.

Constellation uses stateless DX API requests with significant client orchestration. Inspect browser network/timing information and trace the relevant Service REST processing. Request context differs from a traditional stateful portal session; use the trace's step-page context rather than assuming a persistent portal Clipboard.
examples: A lookup is slow only for a large account. Capture its query volume and duration before treating it as a general frontend problem.
After a release, the first use of a rule is slower than repeats. Compare assembly and cache metrics to avoid measuring only the initial compile as steady-state behavior.
A report filters on an unoptimized property inside case data. Confirm the query plan and reporting requirements before optimizing the relevant property and retesting.
For a slow Constellation action, inspect its API request and response, trace the relevant Service REST rule and compare client rendering time with server processing time.
pitfalls: Single tier assumption
Every slow screen is caused by the database.
Locate the tier from actual timings.
Cold versus warm
One first-run timing represents steady-state performance.
Measure comparable cache conditions.
questions: Users report one specific search is slow. What is the best initial diagnostic step?
Reproduce that search and collect timings for the involved tiers
Assume all UI code must be replaced
Double every pool without measurements
Delete all guardrail warnings
A reproducible path and timing evidence locate the cause. Unmeasured blanket changes can miss the actual bottleneck.
An application has a strong guardrail compliance score. Which conclusion remains unsupported?
Every production interaction meets its response-time target
Guardrail checks were considered
Measured performance should still be tested
Warnings can guide improvement
Guardrails reduce design risk, but runtime performance depends on workload and environment as well as rule configuration.
A newly deployed rule is slow on first use but faster on later runs. Which process may explain part of this difference?
Rule assembly and caching
Field auditing always stops after one run
Case authorization disappears
A work queue deletes the rule
First-use generation/compilation and cache warm-up can add cost that differs from subsequent execution.
Why should numerous different ruleset lists be considered in a cache investigation?
Distinct lists can increase rule-cache resource demand
Ruleset lists never affect runtime
Every list is a new database table
They guarantee that no assembly occurs
Rule cache behavior depends on ruleset-list contexts. Excessive diversity can consume additional resources.
A report's PAL delta is dominated by database time. What should the next investigation examine?
The costly SQL operations, predicates and relevant query plan
Only the browser theme
Only the case name
Only the exam duration
Database evidence narrows the next step to the actual statements and access patterns.
A filter on a case-data property triggers a reporting-performance warning. Which response is most appropriate?
Review property optimization and query design, then measure the change
Optimize every property indiscriminately
Ignore data sensitivity and expose all columns
Remove the report without investigating
Optimize according to measured query needs, accounting for storage and security effects rather than blanket changes.
A Constellation user action is slow. Which TWO evidence sources are useful?
Browser network and rendering timings
Trace of the relevant DX Service REST processing
Only a traditional portal's assumed persistent Clipboard
Only a Field Value label
Constellation diagnosis needs client timing and the stateless request's server execution context.
Why is a traditional persistent portal Clipboard assumption unsuitable for every Constellation API request?
Constellation requests are stateless and must be inspected in their own processing context
Constellation never runs server rules
All case data lives only in the browser
DX APIs are always SOAP services
Stateless request processing still uses server rules, but the context must be inspected for the specific API call.

title: Extending UI options
notes: Prefer configured Constellation portals and existing view patterns before custom frontend code. Choose the smallest extension that meets the need. A custom portal experience remains governed by the application's case rules and authorization; grouping related information should preserve useful labels and validation.

Web Embed inserts a Constellation case or page experience into an existing website through generated HTML web-component markup. Configure a Web Embed channel and supported theme options. It uses Constellation rendering rather than giving arbitrary control over every UI implementation detail.

Constellation DX components extend the component library with purpose-specific React components integrated into App Studio view authoring. Use supported APIs and package the component for Pega; only customize when existing patterns do not meet a justified requirement.

Constellation SDKs connect Constellation orchestration to alternative design systems and supported frontend frameworks. They reduce work compared with hand-building every orchestration step, but a custom presentation still needs development, testing and upgrade maintenance.

The Constellation DX API is a model-driven REST interface exposing case data and view metadata. It uses OAuth 2.0. Preserve response eTag and send it as If-Match on updates to protect against stale writes. Handle conflicts by refreshing and reconciling; do not bypass concurrency checks.
examples: A team needs a task-focused portal and grouped contact details. Start with supported portal/view configuration; do not implement a custom design system solely to rearrange a form.
A retailer adds a service-request form to its existing website with a Web Embed channel's generated markup and supported branding settings.
A specialist visual field cannot be expressed by the existing library. Build a supported DX component, upload/package it and verify authoring plus runtime behavior.
A company must use its own React design system. Use the appropriate SDK with the Constellation engine, while keeping case workflow and action metadata governed by Pega.
Fetch assignment action details, render the returned metadata, submit content with the last eTag as If-Match, and refresh when an intervening save causes a conflict.
pitfalls: Embed versus custom frontend
Web Embed is a complete arbitrary design-system SDK.
Choose Web Embed for hosted Pega UI; SDKs for an alternative presentation system.
Data versus metadata
DX responses contain only business fields.
Use view/action metadata as well as case data.
Concurrency
Force an update when If-Match is stale.
Refresh and reconcile instead of overwriting other changes.
questions: A requirement can be met by configuring an existing Constellation portal. Which approach best limits custom maintenance?
Use supported portal and view configuration
Rebuild all case processing in browser code
Create a custom component for every label
Use an unrelated SOAP UI contract
Configuration-first design preserves the supported platform behavior and limits unnecessary customization.
An existing website needs a Pega-rendered case form with limited branding changes. Which option fits?
Constellation Web Embed
A ruleset skim
Database Trace
A work queue
Web Embed places the Constellation experience in an external site using generated web-component markup.
Where is the generated Web Embed markup configured before insertion into a host page?
A Web Embed channel
Only an attachment category
Only an SLA rule
Only a report's filter
The Web Embed channel defines the experience and provides markup for the host website.
One specialized field interaction is missing from the Constellation library. Which extension can integrate it into App Studio authoring?
A supported Constellation DX component
An untrusted script pasted into every form
A Product rule with no UI component
A new Work Group
DX components provide supported component extensions that integrate with view authoring; evaluate existing patterns before building one.
An organization must keep its own design system while using Constellation case orchestration. Which option fits?
A Constellation SDK for the chosen supported framework
Only default Web Embed styling
Only a ruleset prerequisite
Only assignment urgency
SDKs connect Constellation orchestration with an alternative presentation/design system.
Which TWO kinds of information does the model-driven DX response support?
Case data
UI/view metadata and available action information
Only a screenshot of the old portal
An unrestricted bypass of authorization
The API exposes business data and metadata used to render and act on the case. It does not bypass access control.
A fetched case has an eTag. What should an update send to protect against stale writes?
That eTag value in the If-Match request header
A random timestamp invented by the client
Only the portal color
No concurrency header
If-Match carries the previously observed version so the server can detect intervening changes.
An update is rejected after another user saved the case. What is the appropriate client behavior?
Refresh the resource and reconcile the changes
Force an unconditional overwrite
Generate an arbitrary If-Match value
Repeat the stale request indefinitely
A conflict protects another user's persisted changes. Refresh/reconciliation is required; blindly overwriting defeats concurrency control.
Which authentication type is required by the Constellation DX API described in this lesson?
OAuth 2.0
A public anonymous API for every action
A browser theme token
An attachment privilege instead of an authenticated request
Constellation DX API uses OAuth 2.0 authentication. Action and data permissions still govern what an authenticated caller may do.
